newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-IVANISEVIC OVERCOMES SPADEA, HOSTILE CROWD AT LIPTON.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-IVANISEVIC OVERCOMES SPADEA, HOSTILE CROWD AT LIPTON.

text.p: Fourth seed Goran Ivanisevic of Croatia narrowly avoided upset at the Lipton Championships Sunday night, but eked out a win over local favourite Vince Spadea in an ill-tempered third round match.
The unpredictable Croatian fought off Spadea and a hostile crowd to record a 3-6 7-6 6-4 victory.
"They were saying 'damn me' which isn't very nice but then I hit ace. I like it when there is more pressure on me," Ivanisevic said.
Ivanisevic, runner-up here last year, looked sluggish early in the match, throwing in the occasional ace but missing on many of his groundstrokes.
Spadea, from nearby Boca Raton, jumped out to a 5-3 lead and served out the first set with the help of two aces of his own in the final game.
Ivanisevic blew a chance to close out the second set when he squandering a set point at 5-4 by netting a backhand.
But the man who annually hits the most aces on the ATP Tour had the upper hand in the tiebreaker, taking it 7-4 with a backhand volley to send the match into a deciding set.
The atmosphere turned ugly late in the third set when the umpire overruled two apparent Ivanisevic double-faults in the eighth game, each coming at break point for Spadea.
Howls and boos from the partisan crowd over the controversial and critical rulings stopped play briefly before Ivanisevic held serve.
Spadea by then had lost his composure and the fourth seed took advantage.
The American was penalised the first point of the next game for a less than friendly gesture at the umpire and Ivanisevic broke the angry Spadea for a 5-4 lead.
"I got too consumed with what was going on instead of focusing on things I had control of," Spadea said. "I thought I had a lot of opportunities out there that slipped by."
Ivanisevic then belted three more aces in the final game to bring his total to 17, before ending the contest with a backhand winner.
"There were some idiots there in the crowd," Ivanisevic said of the raucous atmosphere.
"But it's a free country and even an idiot can come to watch tennis."
